response.prompt: Rate the Annotation Quality based on each of the following categories.
questionOptions: Is the expected annotation accurately placed?
Is the expected clearly visible without overlap or blurriness?
Is the original chart preserved while adding these annotations?
Are the annotations stylistically consistent with the original chart design?

text-output-base.instruction: Rate how well the model answered the question about this chart.

parameters.taskPrompt: Add visual annotations to mark three key income values on the chart: label $58,746 near the 2006 data point to show the pre-recession level, label $54,569 near the 2012 point to indicate the recovery low, and label $61,372 near the 2017 point to highlight the peak income level.

Add visual annotations to highlight three significant waves: (1) Add a vertical shaded grey region at the left side of the chart with label 'Jan. 2021 peak' at the top marking the initial peak period, (2) Add a vertical shaded grey region in the middle-right area with label 'Delta wave' at the top marking the Delta variant surge around August-October 2021, and (3) Add a vertical shaded grey region at the far right with label 'Omicron wave' at the top marking the Omicron surge in late 2021 to early 2022. The labels should be positioned above the chart area. Return the annotated image.

  text.each(function() {
    let text = d3.select(this),
      words = text.text().split(/\s+/).reverse(),
      word,
      line = [],
      lineNumber = 0,
      lineHeight = 1.2, // ems
      y = text.attr("y"),
      x = text.attr("x"),
      dy = parseFloat(text.attr("dy") || 0),
      tspan = text.text(null).append("tspan").attr("x", x).attr("y", y).attr("dy", dy + "em");
    while (word = words.pop()) {
      line.push(word);
      tspan.text(line.join(" "));
      if (tspan.node().getComputedTextLength() > width) {
        line.pop();
        tspan.text(line.join(" "));
        line = [word];
        tspan = text.append("tspan").attr("x", x).attr("y", y).attr("dy", ++lineNumber * lineHeight + dy + "em").text(word);
      }
    }
  });
}

// Helper: find nearest data point to a target date (for dates not exactly in the weekly series)
function nearestPoint(targetDate) {
  const i = d3.bisector(d => d.date).left(data, targetDate);
  if (i <= 0) return data[0];
  if (i >= data.length) return data[data.length - 1];
  const d0 = data[i - 1], d1 = data[i];
  return (targetDate - d0.date) < (d1.date - targetDate) ? d0 : d1;
}

});
